She actually is starving. I was offering healthy stuff that I eat myself, but it is not good enough to her. Well, I snapped and said "let me know when poverty and starvation lowers your standards". AITA?

This annual cycle can help you develop a greater sense of empathy, compassion, and understanding towards others. As you reflect on your own shortcomings and mistakes, you may become more aware of the importance of forgiveness, both in giving and receiving. This perspective can foster a sense of responsibility, not just to others, but also to yourself, as you strive to become a better version of yourself. Moreover, the annual repetition of these events can help you develop a sense of accountability and personal growth. As you reflect on past experiences and relationships, you may identify areas where you'd like to improve or make amends. This can lead to a greater sense of self-awareness, allowing you to make positive changes and work towards healing and reconciliation in your relationships. Ultimately, the impact of these annual celebrations on your thoughts about what you owe others will depend on your personal experiences, reflections, and intentions. However, by embracing the rhythms and traditions of Christmas and Easter, you're creating a fertile ground for growth, self-reflection, and spiritual exploration.
